name: Cerebras
description:
Cerebras Systems, a pioneering manufacturer of specialized AI processors and computing accelerators, has emerged as one of the most daring players in the semiconductor industry. Known for developing the world's largest computer chip, the Wafer-Scale Engine, the company directly competes with Nvidia's GPUs in the AI space. Since its IPO in May 2026, Cerebras has transitioned from a high-risk startup to a major player in AI infrastructure.
Founded in 2015 by Andrew Feldman, Gary Lauterbach, Michael James, Sean Lie, and Jean-Philippe Fricker—who previously sold their server startup, SeaMicro, to AMD for $334 million—the company took a bold approach by refusing to cut the silicon wafer, instead creating a single chip 58 times larger than any GPU. Despite industry skepticism and burning through up to $8 million per month, Cerebras overcame unprecedented engineering challenges, including cooling a massive chip and addressing microscopic manufacturing defects, to unveil its first functional prototype in July 2019 after investing $200 million.
Originally reliant on its Emirati client G42, Cerebras faced U.S. geopolitical pressures in 2025, prompting a strategic pivot. The company secured landmark contracts with OpenAI and Amazon Web Services (AWS), diversifying its revenue streams and solidifying its independence.
main_investors: Benchmark, Fidelity Investments, Coatue Management, Alpha Wave Global, et Tiger Global

name: Anthropic
description: Societe d'IA generative (famille de modeles Claude). Strategie multi-cloud (AWS, Google Cloud, Azure) et diversification hardware (Nvidia GPU, Amazon Trainium, Google/Broadcom TPU). L'histoire d'Anthropic est intrinsèquement liée à celle d'OpenAI, dont elle est un spin-off direct :Le schisme de 2021 : L'entreprise a été fondée par une fratrie, Dario Amodei (ancien vice-président de la recherche chez OpenAI) et Daniela Amodei (ancienne vice-présidente de la sécurité chez OpenAI). Ils ont quitté OpenAI en emmenant avec eux une équipe d'une dizaine de chercheurs de haut niveau.La divergence idéologique : Les fondateurs d'Anthropic étaient en profond désaccord avec Sam Altman sur la trajectoire d'OpenAI. Ils jugeaient que l'accord commercial de 10 milliards de dollars conclu avec Microsoft en 2019 poussait l'entreprise vers une commercialisation trop rapide, au détriment de la sécurité de l'IA et de l'éthique.Le statut de PBC (2021) : Pour éviter de répéter les erreurs d'OpenAI, Anthropic s'est structurée en Public Benefit Corporation (société à mission d'intérêt public). Ce statut juridique lui permet de placer la sécurité de l'IA au même niveau que la rentabilité financière face à ses actionnaires.La saga "Claude" (2023 - 2026) : En 2023, Anthropic lance son chatbot Claude. Début 2024, la sortie de Claude 3 (Opus) marque un tournant historique en surpassant pour la première fois GPT-4 sur la majorité des benchmarks scientifiques. Les versions successives (Claude 3.5 Sonnet) s'imposent comme les outils préférés des développeurs pour la programmation informatique et l'analyse de données grâce à leur immense "fenêtre de contexte" (capacité de lire des livres entiers en une seule fois).

name: Mistral AI
description:
Mistral AI develops open-source language models and APIs for text generation.
The company was founded in April 2023 by Arthur Mensch (formerly of Google DeepMind), Guillaume Lample, and Timothée Lacroix (both formerly of Meta AI). All three are graduates of École Polytechnique and joined forces to build an independent AI laboratory. In June 2023, just two months after its creation, the startup secured a record seed funding round of €105 million, the largest ever raised in Europe at such an early stage.
By the end of 2023, Mistral AI launched its Mistral 7B model under an open-weight license, disrupting the market with its lightweight design and performance that rivaled much larger closed models. In 2024 and 2025, the company experienced rapid growth, releasing its public platform Le Chat, signing a key commercial partnership with Microsoft Azure, and closing a massive Series C funding round in September 2025 led by semiconductor equipment manufacturer ASML.
In the first half of 2026, Mistral AI began acquiring complementary companies, such as French startup Koyeb and Austrian firm Emmi AI, which specializes in industrial simulations for engineering. At the same time, it announced its Mistral Compute program to build its own sovereign server infrastructure in Europe.
Mistral AI’s strategy is built on a unique hybrid model known on Wall Street as the "Open-Weight Commercial Strategy." The company provides the core of its models for free to developers, fostering organic and widespread adoption while allowing businesses to fine-tune AI directly on their own servers. It also offers a credible European alternative in sovereign AI, addressing strict data confidentiality regulations (GDPR/AI Act) for strategic industries like defense, nuclear, and healthcare. Additionally, Mistral AI focuses on energy and commercial efficiency by developing compact models that require significantly less computational power and memory, drastically reducing operational costs for businesses.

name: Amazon Web Services
description:
Amazon Web Services: The Global Cloud Leader Powering the AI Revolution
Amazon Web Services (AWS), the cloud computing division of Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN), has established itself as the world’s leading on-demand infrastructure provider. Originally launched in 2006, AWS has grown into the company’s most profitable segment, fueled by soaring demand for artificial intelligence and a business model that replaces costly physical infrastructure with pay-as-you-go cloud services.
AWS offers over 200 fully managed services. Its foundational offerings include Amazon EC2, a scalable virtual server solution for application hosting; Amazon S3, a highly secure and scalable object storage service; Amazon RDS, a managed relational database service; and Amazon Bedrock, a platform for AI model development and deployment, leveraging AWS’s proprietary Trainium and Graviton chips.
The rise of generative AI has propelled AWS to unprecedented heights. The division now generates an annualized revenue exceeding $160 billion, with AI-specific services and chips contributing nearly $25 billion to that figure. AWS serves as the primary cloud partner for AI leaders like Anthropic, powering the training and deployment of models such as Claude.
To meet strict GDPR requirements, AWS introduced the European Sovereign Cloud, ensuring that all data from European businesses and institutions remains on the continent under the exclusive control of EU-based personnel.
AWS’s journey began in 2002 with the development of an internal infrastructure SDK for partners. In 2003, Andy Jassy, now Amazon CEO, formalized the vision of a web-based operating system. The official launch of AWS in 2006 introduced S3 for storage and EC2 for virtual servers, pioneering the modern cloud market. In 2015, AWS financials were disclosed for the first time, revealing it as Amazon’s primary profit driver. By 2026, surging AI demand prompted a $220 billion investment in data center infrastructure.
AWS eliminates the need for physical server investments, including hardware, security, and cooling, offering zero upfront costs. It operates on a pay-per-use model, with strict billing based on actual resource consumption, down to the second or hour. The platform provides infinite scalability, allowing users to instantly adjust computing power to handle traffic spikes with a few clicks. Additionally, AWS offers an unmatched catalog depth with over 200 ready-to-use services, from database hosting to seamless AI model integration via Amazon Bedrock.

name: OpenAI
description:
OpenAI: From Altruistic Vision to the AI Powerhouse Shaping the Future
OpenAI is a leading American artificial intelligence research laboratory and technology company, renowned as the global pioneer of generative AI and the creator of the iconic conversational agent ChatGPT.
The story began in December 2015 when a group of Silicon Valley tech leaders, including Sam Altman, Elon Musk, Greg Brockman, and Ilya Sutskever, founded OpenAI during a dinner gathering. Concerned by Google's growing monopoly in AI after its acquisition of DeepMind, they established a non-profit research laboratory with a noble mission: to develop safe, open-source Artificial General Intelligence for the benefit of humanity, backed by $1 billion in initial donation pledges. The original ideal was to publish all patents and source code freely, ensuring that AI advancements would serve the greater good. By February 2018, Elon Musk left the board following strategic disagreements, particularly after the other founders refused to allow Tesla to absorb OpenAI to accelerate its autonomous driving research.
Facing the exorbitant costs of training large language models, Sam Altman executed a dramatic pivot in March 2019. OpenAI created a capped-profit subsidiary to attract private investors while maintaining its non-profit roots. In July 2019, Microsoft saw the opportunity and invested its first $1 billion, becoming OpenAI's exclusive cloud partner through its Azure platform. This funding was primarily used to build massive server infrastructures tailored for AI training rather than covering operational costs. During this period, OpenAI's team published groundbreaking models: GPT-1, GPT-2 (initially withheld from public release due to concerns about potential misuse for disinformation), and GPT-3 in 2020, which laid the foundation for the transformer revolution that would reshape the AI landscape.
The AI landscape changed forever on November 30, 2022, when OpenAI launched ChatGPT, a simple and free chat interface for testing its GPT-3.5 model. The service gained 100 million users in just two months, shattering all previous records for web service adoption. This unprecedented growth forced the tech industry to take notice. In January 2023, Microsoft responded to ChatGPT's success by investing an additional $10 billion and integrating OpenAI's technology into its Bing search engine and Windows operating system through Copilot. March 2023 saw the release of GPT-4, the first truly multimodal model capable of understanding both text and images. GPT-4's performance surpassed human experts in most professional U.S. academic exams, demonstrating a new level of AI capability.
The most dramatic chapter in OpenAI's history unfolded in November 2023, when the original non-profit board, led by Chief Scientist Ilya Sutskever, abruptly fired Sam Altman. The board cited a lack of transparency and concerns that Altman's focus on commercialization was coming at the expense of AI safety. What followed was 100 hours of chaos that would reshape the company's future. Within 48 hours, over 700 of OpenAI's 770 employees signed a letter threatening mass resignation to join Microsoft if Altman wasn't reinstated. The employee revolt left the board with no choice. On November 21, 2023, Altman returned triumphantly to his position as CEO. The board was restructured, with its original members replaced by figures from finance and politics, including Larry Summers, the former U.S. Treasury Secretary. This power struggle marked the definitive victory of the commercial model over the original philanthropic ideal, as OpenAI embraced its role as both a research pioneer and a profitable enterprise.
Entering an era of maturity, OpenAI continued to push boundaries in 2024 with the launch of Sora, an ultra-realistic video generator, and GPT-4o, an AI capable of real-time vocal conversations with human-like emotions and zero latency. The company's focus then shifted toward reasoning models with its o1, o3, and subsequent versions. These advanced models can "think" before responding, solving complex problems in mathematics and programming by generating autonomous internal thought chains. This development brings OpenAI closer to its ultimate goal of achieving Artificial General Intelligence, as the laboratory continues to shape the future of AI while balancing its original altruistic mission with the realities of commercial success.

DeepSeek’s core value proposition is to democratize cutting-edge AI through open-weight models, releasing model weights under the permissive MIT license. The company focuses on hyper-efficient software, leveraging an optimized Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture that enables the training of massive models with minimal hardware. This approach demonstrates that U.S. semiconductor export restrictions can be bypassed, allowing DeepSeek to compete at the highest level despite limited access to advanced chips.

name: Scale AI
description:
Scale AI is one of the invisible yet indispensable pillars of the artificial intelligence revolution. Founded in 2016, the company specializes in sourcing, annotating, cleaning high-quality data, and evaluating models for generative AI. The vast majority of Scale AI’s work is performed by an externalized, non-employee workforce, estimated at tens of thousands or even millions of people, through its two major platforms. Remotasks is a subsidiary focused on mass annotation, particularly for computer vision related to autonomous vehicles, employing freelancers primarily in Southeast Asia (Philippines, India) and Africa. Outlier, on the other hand, is a platform specializing in RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback) for generative AI, recruiting expert profiles (university graduates, linguists, coders) paid by the hour to evaluate and refine model responses.
Founded in 2016 by Alexandr Wang and Lucy Guo within the Y Combinator incubator, Scale AI initially specialized in data labeling for autonomous vehicles before shifting its focus to training and evaluating large language models (LLMs) and generative AI. In June 2025, in a major strategic move, Meta Platforms acquired a 49% non-voting stake for $14.3 billion. Following this deal, founder Alexandr Wang stepped down as CEO to lead Meta’s AI labs. Since August 2026, the company has been led by Francis deSouza, succeeding interim CEO Jason Droege.
Scale AI positions itself as the "fuel supply hub" for AI developers. Its Data Engine enables the collection, sorting, and annotation of raw data at an unprecedented scale for model training. In the RLHF and alignment space, the company relies on thousands of qualified human experts ("Humans-in-the-loop") to refine and align AI behavior. Additionally, Scale AI offers evaluation and security services, including auditing and "Red Teaming" to identify security vulnerabilities and biases in LLMs, in collaboration with leading AI laboratories.

Sakana AI focuses on technological efficiency to overcome the computational brute-force crisis, particularly the scarcity and high cost of GPU chips.
The company’s innovative methods include evolutionary model merging, which uses genetic algorithms to "crossbreed" existing open-source models and produce optimized offspring, avoiding the need to spend hundreds of millions of dollars training models from scratch. Another major breakthrough is The AI Scientist, a system capable of autonomously conducting the entire scientific research cycle—from idea generation and coding to experimentation and report writing.

name: ARM Holdings
description:
Arm Holdings develops CPU architectures and semiconductor IP licensed across mobile, edge, automotive, and data center markets.
Founded in 1990 as Advanced RISC Machines (ARM), it began as a joint venture between Acorn Computers, Apple, and VLSI Technology, with the goal of designing lightweight, energy-efficient microprocessors. Arm went public in 1998 with simultaneous listings on the London Stock Exchange and NASDAQ. Its architecture quickly became the industry standard for mobile phones, starting with the Nokia 6110 and later the iPhone.
In 2016, Japanese conglomerate SoftBank Group acquired Arm for $32 billion, delisting it to accelerate development in the Internet of Things (IoT). Between 2020 and 2022, Nvidia attempted to purchase Arm for $40 billion, but the deal collapsed in early 2022 due to strong opposition from antitrust authorities and Arm’s customers. Arm returned to the public market in 2023 with a NASDAQ listing, marking the largest IPO of the year.
From 2025 to 2026, driven by the generative AI boom, Arm made a historic shift by designing and commercializing its first processors specifically for AI servers and data centers (Agentic CPU / AGI CPU).
Arm’s unique strength lies in its intellectual property (IP) licensing business model. Arm does not produce physical chips but designs the logical architecture (instruction set) and licenses it to third-party manufacturers like Apple, Qualcomm, Nvidia, and Samsung. Its RISC architecture delivers unmatched performance-per-watt efficiency, a critical advantage in the era of AI servers that generate significant heat and consume vast electrical resources. Additionally, Arm earns royalties on every physical chip sold by its licensees, ensuring high-margin, predictable revenue streams.

In February 2026, less than two years after its founding, Black Forest Labs closed a major funding round and deployed its next-generation multimedia models, FLUX.2, capable of object editing and high-definition video generation.
Black Forest Labs applies the same winning formula as Mistral AI but specializes in pixels and visual content. Its B2B-native approach targets enterprises and developers through APIs, with models designed for direct integration into software creation workflows. By distributing high-performance open-weight versions, Black Forest Labs ensures a vast community of creators develops extensions and organically improves the ecosystem. It has also established itself as the white-label supplier for some of the world’s largest content creators, including Adobe and Canva, to enhance their generative AI tool libraries.

Databricks develops a cloud data platform referred to as a 'lakehouse', combining features of data warehouses and data lakes.[59] Unlike traditional proprietary data warehouses, the Databricks architecture processes data while allowing organizations to retain the underlying files in their own cloud storage using open-source formats like Apache Iceberg and Delta Lake.[60] Industry analysts note this separation of compute and storage mitigates vendor lock-in and avoids proprietary data egress fees.[61][62]

The platform is built on the open-source Apache Spark framework, enabling analytical queries on semi-structured data without requiring a traditional database schema.[63] While the platform's classic architecture provided robust distributed computing capabilities, it inherently required data teams to manually configure, size, and manage the underlying cluster infrastructure. To eliminate this operational complexity, Databricks introduced a serverless architecture across its analytics and AI workloads.[64] This serverless tier fully abstracts the cloud environment, automatically provisioning, scaling, and terminating compute resources without requiring manual tuning or cluster management.[65] Databricks had a $5.4 billion revenue run rate

Créer le "cerveau" de la robotique futurePour qu'un robot ou une voiture autonome puisse se déplacer en toute sécurité, il doit comprendre l'espace qui l'entoure. name: UiPath
description:
UiPath is a global software giant specializing in enterprise automation and AI, pioneering Robotic Process Automation (RPA) and agentic AI. Founded in 2005 in Bucharest, Romania, by Daniel Dines and Marius Tîrcă, the company later moved its global headquarters to New York while maintaining a significant presence in Europe, particularly in Germany.
Before its IPO, UiPath raised a total of $1.96 billion across multiple funding rounds (Series A to F), with its last major private round being a $750 million Series F in February 2021. The company went public on the NYSE in April 2021 and currently has a market capitalization of approximately $6.41 billion, after peaking at over $35 billion post-IPO in 2021. UiPath employs 3,981 people worldwide.
UiPath’s value proposition is built on unlocking human potential through end-to-end intelligent automation. Its platform combines RPA software robots with autonomous AI agents capable of understanding screens, reading documents, making complex decisions, and executing repetitive tasks in place of humans. This enables businesses to eliminate time-consuming desk tasks such as data entry, invoice processing, and customer email management, reducing operational costs and minimizing errors. UiPath seamlessly integrates with existing enterprise tools like ERP, CRM, and cloud applications without requiring a complete overhaul of their IT infrastructure.

name: Recursion Pharmaceuticals

Its Recursion Operating System (OS), a platform based on various technologies, allows the company to map and explore billions of biological and chemical relationships within the Recursion data universe. The company integrates physical and digital components as iterative loops of atoms and bits, scaling biological and chemical data from traditional laboratories, organized into virtuous cycles using computational tools, to quickly translate in silico hypotheses into validated knowledge and innovative chemistry. Its clinical programs in oncology and rare diseases include REC-617, REC-1245, REC-3565 and REC-4539. Its REC-617 is an orally administered cyclin-dependent kinase 7 (CDK7) inhibitor for the treatment of advanced solid tumors. Its REV102 program targets ectonucleotide pyrophosphatase/phosphodiesterase 1 (ENPP1), an enzyme involved in the pathogenesis of PPH.

name: Multiverse Computing
description:
Multiverse a été cofondée en 2019 par Enrique Lizaso, Román Orús, Alfonso Rubio et Sam Mugel. Lizaso, trésorière et membre du conseil d'administration du Consortium européen pour l'industrie quantique, et Orús, professeur de recherche Ikerbasque au Donostia International Physics Center et ancien boursier Marie Curie à l'Institut Max Planck d'optique quantique, discutaient sur WhatsApp lorsque l'idée de créer une entreprise de calcul quantique pour la finance a vu le jour[1].

En 2021, l'entreprise a annoncé un financement de 12,5 millions d'euros via le programme Accélérateur du Conseil européen de l'innovation (EIC). Par la suite, en 2024, elle a clôturé un tour de table de 25 millions d'euros, atteignant une valorisation de 100 millions d'euros. Plus tard dans la même année, la start-up a été sélectionnée par le Scaling Club de l'EIC – qui dispose d'un budget de 10 milliards de dollars – comme l'une des 48 entreprises qui bénéficieront d'un soutien en matière de financement, de mentorat et de mise en place de partenariats stratégiques.

En avril 2022, l'entreprise s'est associée à la Banque du Canada pour étudier comment l'informatique quantique peut simuler l'adoption des cryptomonnaies. Ces recherches ont fait du Canada le premier pays du G7 à explorer le modèle des réseaux complexes et des cryptomonnaies à l'aide de l'informatique quantique. Plus tard dans l'année, BASF a utilisé Singularity de Multiverse pour développer des modèles visant à optimiser les opérations de change entre les devises américaines et européennes[2].

Parmi les autres organisations qui explorent le logiciel quantique de Multiverse, on peut citer BBVA, Crédit Agricole CIB et Repsol[1],[3],[4]. En 2022, Gartner a désigné Multiverse Computing comme « Gartner Cool Vendor » pour avoir proposé « des technologies et des services logiciels quantiques permettant l'intégration de l'exploration de solutions quantiques dans le secteur des services financiers ».

L'entreprise a lancé CompactifAI, sa technologie de compression de modèles d'IA, en 2023 [5] afin de compresser des modèles d'IA tels que les LLM. CompactifAI utilise des réseaux de tenseurs pour réduire le nombre de paramètres d'un modèle, ce qui diminue sa taille totale et réduit les besoins en mémoire et en espace de stockage. Cela réduit l'empreinte globale des modèles, les rendant plus portables et plus faciles à exécuter en périphérie dans des applications telles que les véhicules autonomes et les installations de production distantes.

En septembre 2024, l'entreprise a été sélectionnée par Amazon Web Services (AWS) pour participer à son programme mondial « AWS Generative AI Accelerator 2024 »[6]. Ce programme consistait en un parcours de 10 semaines qui a débuté au siège d'Amazon à Seattle, avec des sessions de formation et de mentorat qui se sont conclues par une présentation lors de la conférence AWS re:Invent à Las Vegas, dans le Nevada.

Multiverse Computing a clôturé son tour de table de série B de 215 millions de dollars en juin 2025[7]. La série B a été menée par Bullhound Capital, HP Tech Ventures, SETT, Forgepoint Capital International, CDP Venture Capital, Santander Climate VC, Toshiba et Capital Riesgo de Euskadi-Grupo SPRI a également participé au tour de table. Ce nouvel investissement visait à développer les modèles d'IA compressés de CompactifAI, qui sont des versions hautement compressées des principaux grands modèles de langage (LLM) open source. Ils conservent la précision d'origine, sont 4 à 12 fois plus rapides et permettent une réduction de 50 % à 80 % des coûts d'inférence. Ces modèles compressés, abordables et économes en énergie peuvent être exécutés dans le cloud, dans des centres de données privés ou, dans le cas des LLM ultra-compressés, directement sur des appareils tels que des ordinateurs, des téléphones, des voitures, des drones et même des Raspberry Pi[8].

Its mission is to improve the lives of patients who have undergone laryngectomy (larynx removal due to cancer) or are on mechanical ventilation by eliminating the complications and discomfort of traditional voice prostheses.
Altavo’s breakthrough "Silent Speech" technology uses AI and non-invasive radar sensors to restore natural-sounding voices to people who have lost their ability to speak. The system captures invisible movements of the throat and lips using micro-radar sensors placed on the skin. Machine learning algorithms then instantly convert these radar signals into a real-time, fluid, and personalized synthetic voice.
Unlike conventional implants, Altavo’s approach is fully non-invasive, eliminates surgical infection risks, and delivers a significantly more natural sound quality compared to robotic voices.

Our goal is to close the information gap, create transparency, and help governments worldwide make well-informed decisions about China. Its clients include government agencies, defense organizations, and compliance and corporate users. Datenna also conducts research on European acquisitions by Chinese investors.
History
Datenna was founded in 2017 by Jaap van Etten and Edward Brinkmann. Van Etten had previously worked as a Dutch diplomat, serving as a Science and Technology Attaché at the Dutch embassy in Beijing before launching the company.
Datenna received a soft loan from the Netherlands Enterprise Agency, part of the Dutch government, in 2017.
In 2020, Datenna research showed that the Chinese government had a stake in 53% of Swiss companies acquired by Chinese firms since 2010. The Ultimate Beneficial Owner in these Swiss acquisitions was either part of the Chinese government or the Chinese government held a substantial but non-controlling stake in the acquiring company. In February 2025, Alex Younger, former Chief of the British Secret Intelligence Service (MI6), joined the company's advisory board.

name: Luo Automation
description: To guarantee patient safety, every single injectable medicine must be visually inspected. Therefore, hospital pharmacies and pharmaceutical companies check every vial, syringe or ampoule to make sure it’s free of defects. Defects can be contaminations such as glass or steel particles, but can also be a broken cap, a big crack or a small dent. In general, this visual inspection is done by hand. Every container must be evaluated for 10 seconds by a trained operator. For companies that produce big batches and lots of similar products (more than 5 million containers per year) it’s feasible to automate this process. To do so, expensive machinery (>2M euro) is bought, an extensive training process is started and after the installation and validation process, one or two products can be visually inspected. However, lots of companies do not produce enough containers per year to account a 2M euro investment or have a very diverse product portfolio, which makes current machinery not suitable. As a result, in Europe more than 1.2 billion containers are checked by hand. Every year. Luo tries to bridge the gap between huge, conservative and expensive machinery and the manual operation. Besides developing the hardware (machine) that is needed to gather the necessary data of every container, Luo uses different AI and Machine Learning models to analyze this data and define if the container is good or needs to be rejected. One of the key challenges in this field, is that defect data of syringes, ampoules and vials is barely available. Even if a decent defect set is available for one specific medicine in one specific container with one specific filling volume, this is not applicable on other medicines or other containers. Luo is using innovative training methods to make sure we are able to find defects the algorithm has never seen before. For the visual inspection of one container, about 8 (!) different anomaly detection models are used. These models are trained with normal data, to make sure the models are not dependent on defect data. By using these innovative models, we are able quickly adapt to new medicine or new containers. As a result, it’s feasible to automate the obligatory visual inspection for small batches or a diverse product portfolio as well. Besides saving a lot of valuable time of healthcare professionals, this increase the consistency and quality of the product and provides insights in production quality over time.

description:
Alphabet Inc. is a multinational technology holding company and the parent company of Google, as well as other businesses such as YouTube, Waymo, and Google DeepMind.
Founded in 1998 by Larry Page and Sergey Brin in a Menlo Park garage, Google revolutionized internet search with its PageRank algorithm. The company went public in 2004 at $85 per share, a historic IPO, and shortly after launched Gmail (2004) while acquiring YouTube (2006) and Android (2005). In 2015, a major restructuring led to the creation of Alphabet Inc., with Google becoming a subsidiary. This allowed the company to separate its core businesses—Search, YouTube, and Cloud—from its forward-looking investments, known as Other Bets. In 2019, Sundar Pichai succeeded the founders as CEO of the entire Alphabet group.
Between 2023 and 2026, Alphabet made a massive pivot toward generative AI, merging Google Brain and DeepMind. Its ecosystem now revolves around multimedia models like Gemini and AI Overviews, which provide direct answers in search results.
Alphabet’s business is built on three main pillars: organizing the world’s information to make it universally accessible and useful through leading platforms such as Search, Maps, Android, and YouTube, which reach billions of people; powering targeted advertising by offering the world’s most powerful ad infrastructure (Google Ads) based on precise purchase intent; and driving cloud and AI transformation by accelerating the digital transition of businesses through Google Cloud and selling massive AI-powered computing capabilities.

ByteDance is a global internet company founded in March 2012 in Beijing by entrepreneur Zhang Yiming. It is the parent company of TikTok and its Chinese counterpart, Douyin, and has grown into the world's largest privately held unicorn. The company initially achieved success in China with its content aggregator, Toutiao, followed by the short-form video app Douyin in 2016. ByteDance expanded globally in 2017 with the launch of TikTok and the acquisition of Musical.ly, merging the two platforms.
In 2025 and 2026, ByteDance significantly shifted its focus toward generative AI, deploying its chatbot, Doubao, and advanced video models like Seedance 2.0/2.5 and OmniHuman-1. To avoid a total ban, TikTok had to sever its direct operational ties with China by completely restructuring its U.S. operations.
ByteDance's value proposition is built on its ultra-high-performance AI-driven recommendation algorithm, widely regarded as the most addictive and precise in the market. It captures user attention through engaging short-form video content and monetizes its audience in three ways: precision-targeted advertising on TikTok and Douyin, social commerce through TikTok Shop (integrating video entertainment with in-app shopping), and enterprise and consumer AI tools, including automated video generation, LLMs, and conversational agents.

Contrairement à une startup classique, ses chiffres et son histoire sont marqués par un basculement réglementaire historique. L’entreprise trouve ses racines en 2004 avec le lancement d'Alipay, le système de paiement créé par Jack Ma pour sécuriser les transactions sur la plateforme e-commerce d'Alibaba. En octobre 2014, cette branche a été séparée pour devenir une entité financière autonome sous le nom de Ant Financial, avant d'être rebaptisée Ant Group en 2020.L'entreprise a marqué l'histoire financière mondiale en novembre 2020 lorsque son introduction en bourse (IPO) simultanée à Shanghai et Hong Kong (qui devait être la plus grande de l'histoire à 35 milliards de dollars) a été suspendue à la dernière minute par les régulateurs chinois. En 2024, afin d'accélérer son développement et de s'adapter à cette nouvelle ère, l'entreprise a scindé ses activités en accordant leur indépendance opérationnelle à trois entités clés, dont son bras armé international, Ant International, basé à Singapour. La proposition de valeur d'Ant Group repose sur la fourniture d'une infrastructure numérique financière tout-en-un, combinant les paiements, le crédit de masse, la gestion de fortune et l'IA d'entreprise :Alipay & Alipay+ : Un écosystème de paiement mobile universel qui connecte des centaines de millions de marchands à des dizaines de portefeuilles numériques transfrontaliers à l'international.Démocratisation du crédit et des services (B2B/B2C) : Financement instantané via des algorithmes prédictifs sans garantie physique traditionnelle, complété par l'IA (Antom Copilot agissant comme un directeur financier virtuel pour les PME).Technologies de confiance (TechFirst) : Commercialisation de sa base de données distribuée OceanBase et de ses outils blockchain pour moderniser les banques et entreprises mondiales.

name: Intel
description: L'histoire d'Intel se découpe en trois grandes ères industrielles :La fondation et l'âge d'or (1968 - 2010s) : Créée par Gordon Moore (père de la "Loi de Moore") et Robert Noyce, Intel invente le microprocesseur commercialisé en 1971. Grâce au partenariat historique "Wintel" (Windows + Intel), l'entreprise s'impose comme le moteur absolu des ordinateurs personnels et des serveurs mondiaux pendant quatre décennies.La décennie de crise et les retards technologiques (2015 - 2024) : Intel rate le virage des puces pour smartphones (refusant initialement de produire la puce de l'iPhone). L'entreprise accumule ensuite d'importants retards de gravure (les "nœuds" technologiques), laissant le taïwanais TSMC prendre la tête de la fabrication mondiale, tandis que ses concurrents AMD (sur les PC/serveurs) et Nvidia (sur l'IA) gagnent d'immenses parts de marché.Le grand redressement (2025 - 2026) : Sous l'impulsion d'une nouvelle gouvernance (menée par le CEO Lip-Bu Tan), d'investissements massifs du gouvernement américain (CHIPS Act) et de partenariats majeurs (notamment avec Nvidia et Apple), Intel orchestre un retournement spectaculaire. Après des années difficiles, ses revenus ont bondi de plus de 25 % sur un an à la mi-2026, portés par l'explosion de la demande en infrastructures IA. La proposition de valeur d'Intel a été profondément restructurée pour répondre aux exigences de l'ère de l'intelligence artificielle. Elle s'articule aujourd'hui autour de trois piliers principaux :A. La souveraineté industrielle mondiale (Intel Foundry)Intel se positionne comme le seul fondeur occidental capable de fabriquer des puces à la pointe de la technologie (gravure à l'échelle de l'Angström, notamment le nœud de fabrication Intel 18A) sur le sol américain et européen. Face aux risques géopolitiques pesant sur Taïwan (TSMC), Intel offre une sécurité d'approvisionnement cruciale pour les gouvernements et les géants de la Tech.B. L'orchestration CPU pour l'IA et les centres de donnéesPlutôt que de chercher à remplacer les processeurs graphiques (GPU) de Nvidia, Intel a maximisé la valeur de ses propres processeurs de serveurs (comme la gamme Xeon 6). Ces puces sont devenues indispensables en tant que contrôleurs hôtes au sein des architectures de serveurs d'IA de premier plan (comme le système Nvidia DGX Reuben) pour orchestrer les flux de données massifs.C. Le leadership de l'architecture "AI PC"Pour le grand public et les entreprises, Intel mène la transition vers le PC IA. Ses processeurs intègrent nativement des NPU (Neural Processing Units) haut de gamme. Cela permet d'exécuter des modèles d'IA générative et des agents autonomes localement sur l'ordinateur, sans dépendre du cloud, garantissant ainsi rapidité et confidentialité. Pour réussir sa transformation, Intel a séparé ses activités en deux branches distinctes (le modèle IDM 2.0) :BrancheRôle principalPerformance récente (2026)Intel ProductsConçoit et vend des puces pour PC (Client Computing Group) et des serveurs d'IA (Data Center & AI).Représente la majorité des profits, tirée par la hausse des prix des puces IA premiums.Intel FoundryFabrique des puces pour le compte d'Intel, mais aussi pour des clients tiers (concepteurs "fabless").En pleine accélération grâce à des discussions de partenariats stratégiques (ex: Apple).

name: Berkshire Hathaway
description:
Berkshire Hathaway, originally founded in 1955 as a textile manufacturer and transformed into an investment conglomerate in 1965 under Warren Buffett, is now led by CEO Greg Abel since January 2026. The company does not raise external funds but generates its own capital, holding a record cash reserve of nearly $400 billion as of summer 2026. With a market capitalization of approximately $1.1 trillion (as of August 2026), its Class A shares (BRK.A) trade at over $760,000 each. The conglomerate employs 388,000 people globally, with only about 30 at its Omaha headquarters and the rest across its subsidiaries, such as Geico, Duracell, and Berkshire Hathaway Energy.
Under Greg Abel, Berkshire Hathaway is making strategic investments in AI infrastructure:


AI Infrastructure Investments: Berkshire focuses on hardware and computing infrastructure rather than software. In June 2026, it invested an additional $10 billion in Alphabet (Google) to support the expansion of its AI data centers, making Alphabet its fifth-largest stock holding. Berkshire also benefits indirectly from Apple’s global deployment of Apple Intelligence through iPhones and Macs.


Energy Supply for Data Centers: Berkshire Hathaway Energy (BHE) is capitalizing on the massive electricity demand from AI data centers. In key states like Iowa, data centers already consume nearly 8% of the grid’s peak capacity. Abel plans to expand energy infrastructure by 50% over the next five years to power AI computing, ensuring tech giants cover the full cost.


Narrow AI Integration in Subsidiaries: Berkshire adopt AI only if it delivers immediate ROI in safety, efficiency, or cost reduction.

Insurance (GEICO): AI accelerates claims processing, detects fraud, and analyzes deepfake threats.
Railroad (BNSF): Predictive algorithms optimize rail yard management and analyze wheel wear to prevent derailments.

L'entreprise développe sa première puce de mémoire DRAM.1992 : Samsung devient le n°1 mondial des puces mémoire (DRAM), une position qu'elle n'a plus jamais quittée.2006 : La marque détrône Sony et devient le premier fabricant mondial de téléviseurs.2012 : Elle dépasse Nokia pour devenir le premier vendeur mondial de smartphones.2024-2026 : Restructuration majeure des usines de puces. Intégration verticale de pointe : C'est la force absolue de l'entreprise. Contrairement à Apple qui sous-traite toute sa production, Samsung Electronics conçoit et fabrique ses propres écrans OLED, ses capteurs photo, ses processeurs et ses puces de mémoire. Elle vend d'ailleurs ces composants à ses propres concurrents.Double positionnement de marché :Grand public (Division DX) : Des smartphones (gammes de prix de l'entrée de gamme Galaxy A jusqu'aux fleurons pliants Galaxy Z), des téléviseurs haut de gamme (QLED/OLED) et de l'électroménager connecté.Industriel et composants (Division DS) : Fournisseur clé de l'infrastructure technologique mondiale grâce à ses usines de fonderie de puces et de puces mémoires haute performance nécessaires aux calculs d'IA.

Meta
description:
Meta (formerly Facebook Inc.) is an American multinational technology company founded in 2004 by Mark Zuckerberg under the name TheFacebook. Now a tech giant, it owns platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Messenger, and Threads. Its business model relies on advertising for 98% of its revenue, while heavily investing in strategic areas: open-source artificial intelligence (Llama models, Meta AI assistant), virtual and augmented reality hardware (Meta Quest headsets, Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses), and custom silicon (MTIA chip program). In 2025, its revenue reached $201 billion, with a market capitalization estimated at $1.8 trillion as of mid-2026.
Meta’s history includes key milestones: after opening to the public and going public in 2012 at $38 per share, the company experienced rapid external growth with the acquisition of Instagram for $1 billion in 2012 and WhatsApp for $21 billion in 2014. In 2018, the Cambridge Analytica scandal, involving a personal data leak, led to a major overhaul of its privacy policies. In 2021, the group officially adopted the name Meta, symbolizing its pivot toward the metaverse. Since 2023, it has focused on AI, launching Threads to compete with X (formerly Twitter) and developing generative AI models to make them accessible to all.
Meta’s strategy revolves around three pillars: connecting over 3.6 billion daily users across its apps, providing ultra-effective advertising tools to businesses—particularly its 9 million SME partners—through AI, and driving innovation in disruptive technologies, such as virtual and augmented reality via its Reality Labs division, or generative AI, which it aims to make "superintelligent" and open to everyone.

name: Y combinator
description:
Fondation (2005) : Créé à Boston par Paul Graham, Jessica Livingston, Robert Morris et Trevor Blackwell. Le concept révolutionnaire introduit le financement standardisé de "cohortes" (batches) de startups.Déménagement (2009) : YC centralise ses activités dans la Silicon Valley (Mountain View) pour se rapprocher du cœur de l'écosystème tech.Ère Sam Altman (2014-2019) : Sous sa présidence, l'accélérateur change d'échelle, augmente drastiquement la taille des promotions et crée le fonds YC Continuity pour investir dans les phases ultérieures de ses pépites.Ère Garry Tan (Depuis 2023) : Reprenant les rênes comme CEO, il recentre YC sur l'amorçage au cœur de San Francisco et ferme le fonds de croissance pour se concentrer sur les fondateurs techniques, notamment dans la vague de l'Intelligence Artificielle native. 
Y Combinator (YC) est le plus célèbre et le plus influent accélérateur de startups au monde, ayant propulsé des géants technologiques comme Airbnb, Dropbox, Stripe, Reddit, Coinbase et Instacart.🚀 Fonctionnement et ModèleInvestissement standard : YC investit un montant fixe (actuellement 500 000 $) dans chaque startup sélectionnée en échange d'une participation au capital (généralement 7 % de parts fixes, plus un complément sous forme de SAFE).Le programme des "Batches" : Deux fois par an (sessions d'hiver Winter et d'été Summer), des centaines d'entrepreneurs rejoignent un programme intensif de 3 mois basé en Silicon Valley (Californie).Le Demo Day : Le programme se clôture par un événement ultra-sélectif où les fondateurs pitchent leur projet devant les plus grands investisseurs en capital-risque (VC) de la planète pour lever des fonds.🎯 Valeur ajoutée uniqueLe réseau d'Alumni : L'accès à une communauté ultra-puissante de plus de 10 000 fondateurs à travers le monde, facilitant l'entraide, le recrutement et l'acquisition des premiers clients.Le tampon de crédibilité : Être sélectionné par YC (le taux d'acceptation est inférieur à 2 %) agit comme un label de qualité suprême qui valide le projet aux yeux des investisseurs et du marché.L'école de la vitesse : Le programme enseigne une méthodologie stricte axée sur deux priorités absolues : concevoir un produit que les gens veulent (Make something people want) et parler à ses utilisateurs.

name: Cisco
description:
In 1984, Leonard Bosack and Sandy Lerner, a couple of Stanford University scientists, founded Cisco in San Francisco. They invented the first multiprotocol router, enabling heterogeneous computer networks to communicate with each other.
Cisco went public on the NASDAQ in 1990. At the peak of the dot-com bubble in 2000, it briefly became the world’s most valuable company, with a market capitalization of $555 billion, symbolizing the backbone of the web’s infrastructure. Between 2003 and 2015, the company diversified beyond routers through major acquisitions such as Linksys (consumer networking) and Webex (videoconferencing). After 20 years of leadership, John Chambers handed over the reins to Chuck Robbins.
In 2024-2025, Cisco made a historic acquisition of cybersecurity firm Splunk for $28 billion, marking a major strategic shift toward software and recurring subscription models. By 2026, demand for its AI-dedicated hardware infrastructure surged, with record order books from cloud giants (hyperscalers).
Cisco designs and sells the networking hardware (switches, routers) that routes nearly all of the world’s enterprise and telecom data, making it the backbone of the internet. The company protects these network infrastructures with a comprehensive cybersecurity catalog and advanced data analytics management, powered by Splunk’s technologies and full-stack observability solutions. With its Silicon One chip range and ultra-fast data center switches, Cisco enables the connection of thousands of GPUs required to train generative AI models without bottlenecks.
main_investors: Vanguard Group (~9,3 % des actions), BlackRock (~8,1 % des actions), State Street Corporation (~4,8 % des actions).

name: Samsung
description:
In 1938, Lee Byung-chul founded Samsung Sanghoe in Daegu as a small trading shop exporting dried fish, vegetables, and noodles to China. After the Korean War, in 1954, he diversified into industrial activities by opening the country’s largest wool mill, Cheil Industries. In 1969, Samsung made a strategic entry into the technology sector with the creation of its subsidiary, Samsung Electronics. By 1974, it launched Samsung Heavy Industries, investing heavily in shipbuilding and petrochemicals.
Between 1990 and 2000, the group constructed three of the world’s tallest skyscrapers: the Petronas Towers in Malaysia, Taipei 101 in Taiwan, and the Burj Khalifa in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. By 2026, Samsung modernized all its subsidiaries—ranging from biotech to insurance and shipbuilding—by integrating autonomous artificial intelligence infrastructures.
Samsung is more than just a phone brand; it is a vast ecosystem of over 60 interconnected companies with cross-holdings, forming a chaebol. In South Korea, it supports citizens "from cradle to grave" through its hospitals, insurance companies, residential complexes, and amusement parks. The group ensures South Korea’s economic sovereignty by mastering critical global industries: high technology (chips and displays), heavy shipbuilding (LNG carriers), complex civil engineering, and biopharmaceuticals.
In high technology, Samsung Electronics competes globally with Apple, TSMC, Sony, Intel, and LG. In biotechnology, Samsung Biologics rivals Lonza (Switzerland), Catalent (USA), and Boehringer Ingelheim (Germany). In construction and engineering, Samsung C&T and Samsung E&A face competition from Vinci (France), China State Construction (China), and Bechtel (USA). In shipbuilding, Samsung Heavy Industries competes with HD Hyundai Heavy Industries (South Korea) and CSSC (China). In insurance and finance, Samsung Life and Fire & Marine go up against Hanwha Life (South Korea), AXA (France), and Allianz (Germany).

name: Semrush
description: Semrush est une plateforme SaaS de référence mondiale dédiée au marketing digital, principalement reconnue pour son expertise en optimisation pour les moteurs de recherche (SEO), en analyse concurrentielle et en visibilité en ligne. Fondée en 2008, elle centralise plus de 55 outils avancés indispensables pour les professionnels du web, les agences et les entreprises

name: Bosch Ventures
description: Bosch Ventures (anciennement connu sous le nom officiel de Robert Bosch Venture Capital GmbH) est la filiale de capital-risque d'entreprise (Corporate Venture Capital) du groupe allemand Robert Bosch GmbH. Fondé en 2007, ce fonds investit à l'échelle mondiale dans des start-up technologiques de rupture, principalement aux stades d'amorçage (Seed), Series A, B et C. Actifs sous gestion (AUM) : Bosch Ventures gère un portefeuille global d'environ 1,1 à 1,3 milliard de dollars répartis sur plusieurs structures de fonds successives.

name: 5C
description:
5C Group is one of the largest providers of AI digital infrastructure in North America. Formed through the merger of Hypertec Cloud and 5C Data Centers, the company designs and deploys the physical architecture required for cutting-edge research labs and major AI enterprises, including data centers, high-performance computing (HPC) clusters, and AI factories.
The 5C Model
The group’s name is built on five core pillars embedded in its technological strategy:

Customization: Tailored design of infrastructure stacks (compute, cooling, networking).
Celerity: Record-speed deployment and commissioning.
Cutting Edge: Integration of high-performance computing (HPC) and immersion cooling to manage heat dissipation from chips.
Climate: Reduction of the water and energy footprint of supercomputers.
Cost Efficiency: Financial optimization of training and inference workloads.
Scale and Power

Massive Capacity: The group has a roadmap of over 2 gigawatts (GW) of power to support hundreds of thousands of GPUs.

Major Financing: 5C Group has secured $835 million in capital from investors such as Brookfield and Deutsche Bank to fuel its global expansion.

name: 2CRSI
description: 2CRSi est un groupe technologique français, basé à Strasbourg, spécialisé dans la conception et la fabrication de serveurs informatiques éco-conçus et de solutions de calcul haute performance (HPC) adaptés aux charges de travail de l'intelligence artificielle.

name: Lightspeed
description:
Lightspeed AI is an advanced conversational and agentic intelligence layer natively integrated into the Lightspeed Commerce platform. It enables retail, restaurant, and hospitality operators to bypass complex data dashboards and query their business metrics using natural language. Retail Operations
The system enables merchants to query data conversationally, such as "What were my bestsellers by margin last weekend?", and receive contextual answers instead of raw spreadsheets. It also automates online presence through the AI Showroom, transforming in-store product catalogs into e-commerce digital showrooms by generating custom descriptions and removing photo backgrounds. Additionally, AI Invoice OCR uses optical character recognition to read supplier packing slips or invoices, automatically generating purchase orders and eliminating manual inventory entry.
Restaurant & Hospitality Management
The platform optimizes menus by automatically identifying low-performing items to reduce food waste and highlighting high-margin options to guide cross-selling. It also tracks server metrics to optimize staffing by identifying peak performance hours and maximizing shifts. Service pacing data feeds into internal dashboards like Tempo to monitor and adjust how quickly guests are served.
Recreational Dealerships (DMS)
The AI Command Center serves as a specialized insights engine for powersports, marine, and RV dealerships. It evaluates real-time business performance and delivers predictive recommendations by comparing individual metrics against historical and network-wide data trends.

Salesforce
description: Salesforce, le géant mondial du CRM (gestion de la relation client) basé à San Francisco, s'est imposé comme un acteur incontournable de la Tech médicale et de l'intelligence artificielle. À travers sa suite dédiée Health Cloud et sa nouvelle plateforme Agentforce Health, Salesforce n'agit pas comme un outil de diagnostic clinique (comme Dermalyser ou StratifAI), mais comme le cerveau opérationnel, administratif et d'engagement qui connecte les hôpitaux, les patients et les laboratoires pharmaceutiques. 1999 (Fondation) : Création à San Francisco par Marc Benioff (ancien cadre d'Oracle) et Parker Harris. L'entreprise naît avec une idée révolutionnaire pour l'époque : remplacer les logiciels lourds à installer par des logiciels accessibles directement sur internet, inventant le concept de Cloud Computing et de SaaS (Software as a Service).2004 : Introduction en bourse (NYSE).2018 - 2021 (L'ère des méga-acquisitions) : Pour étendre son empire, Salesforce rachète MuleSoft (intégration de données) pour 6,5 milliards $, Tableau Software (analyse de données) pour 15,7 milliards \(, et enfin **Slack** (messagerie collaborative) pour 27,7 milliards \).2024 - 2026 (Le virage de l'IA Agentique) : Après avoir intégré l'IA prédictive (Einstein), l'entreprise pivote massivement vers l'IA autonome en lançant Agentforce. Ce virage marque la transition d'un simple CRM à un écosystème géré par des agents intelligents. La promesse centrale de Salesforce est de regrouper toutes les données d'une entreprise sur une plateforme unique appelée Customer 360 afin de piloter la relation client de bout en bout.Ses forces reposent sur quatre piliers :Unification des services : Vente (Sales Cloud), service client (Service Cloud), marketing (Marketing Cloud), et commerce en ligne (Commerce Cloud) partagent la même donnée.IA Agentique (Agentforce) : Permet aux entreprises de déployer des agents virtuels autonomes capables de résoudre des tâches complexes (support client, prise de commande, gestion de dossiers médicaux) 24h/24 sans intervention humaine.Personnalisation sectorielle : Des versions hautement spécialisées, comme Health Cloud, répondent directement aux exigences de conformité et aux processus métiers de secteurs pointus (comme la médecine et la pharmacie).

name: Shopify
description:
In 2004-2006, Tobias Lütke, Daniel Weinand, and Scott Lake founded their company in Ottawa. Frustrated by the limitations of existing software while trying to launch their own snowboard online store, they decided to build their own e-commerce platform. It was officially launched as Shopify in June 2006.
Shopify went public in 2015 with a simultaneous IPO on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) and the Toronto Stock Exchange. During the Covid-19 pandemic in 2020-2022, Shopify experienced phenomenal growth, establishing itself as the primary alternative to Amazon for independent merchants. In 2023, the company underwent a major restructuring, selling its logistics arm (Deliverr) to Flexport to refocus exclusively on its core business: e-commerce software.
By 2025-2026, Shopify transitioned into the era of AI-powered commerce. Artificial intelligence has become the central engine of the platform, transforming store administration into a simple conversation. The company consolidated its technologies into two major free offerings for all merchants: Shopify Magic for creation and Shopify Sidekick for action. The integration of Sidekick and Agentic Storefronts technology enabled full automation of inventory management, marketing, and customer service through autonomous agents.
Shopify’s value proposition revolves around simplifying store creation, allowing anyone—from small businesses and creators to multinational corporations like Mattel—to design an e-commerce site without prior technical expertise. It offers seamless omnichannel capabilities, centralizing sales on a single dashboard whether they come from websites, social media platforms (Instagram, TikTok), mobile apps (Shop App), or physical stores (via Shopify POS). Additionally, Shopify provides one of the world’s fastest and most efficient one-click payment systems, Shop Pay, which can increase shopping cart conversion rates by up to 15%.

name: PhotoRoom
description:
réée en 2019 et basée à Paris, la startup PhotoRoom révolutionne l'édition de photos grâce à l'intelligence artificielle. La plateforme s'adresse aux petites entreprises, créateurs et revendeurs e-commerce souhaitant créer des visuels professionnels en quelques clics. Les outils développés permettent de supprimer l'arrière-plan, retoucher les images, ajouter du texte ou redimensionner les visuels. PhotoRoom propose également des API permettant d'automatiser les productions créatives et d'intégrer ses fonctionnalités directement dans d'autres applications.

L'entreprise connaît une croissance exponentielle avec 150 millions de téléchargements et 5 milliards d'images modifiées depuis sa création. PhotoRoom a levé 19 millions de dollars en novembre 2022, puis 43 millions de dollars en février 2024 auprès de Balderton Capital et Aglaé Ventures, portant son financement total à 64 millions de dollars pour une valorisation de 500 millions de dollars. Comptant 60 salariés, la startup a développé son propre modèle de diffusion pour générer des images à partir de texte, plus rapide que Midjourney ou Dall-E. Son API équipe déjà les produits de Netflix, Shopify et Printify, permettant à des millions d'utilisateurs de créer des visuels de qualité studio divisant par dix le temps d'édition.

name: Dust
description:
Dust est une startup spécialisée dans la création d'assistants IA personnalisés pour les entreprises. Cofondée en 2023 par Stanislas Polu et Gabriel Hubert, cette société se positionne comme acteur incontournable de l'intelligence artificielle générative en France avec l'ambition de révolutionner le travail en équipe. Dust se démarque par ses solutions innovantes et performantes pour améliorer la collaboration et la productivité des employés.

Pour développer ses agents intelligents, la startup utilise les données internes des entreprises issues de logiciels tels que Google Drive, Slack et GitHub, associées aux modèles d'IA les plus performants comme OpenAI et Anthropic. Dust emploie 59 salariés basés à Paris. En 2024, la société a bouclé une levée de fonds de 5 millions d'euros pour améliorer ses capacités en matière d'automatisation intelligente et renforcer son équipe technique.

name: Gleamer
description:
In 2017, Christian Allouche, Alexis Ducarouge, and Dr. Nor-Eddine Regnard founded Gleamer to address a critical gap in healthcare: while demand for medical imaging had doubled over a decade in OECD countries, the number of radiologists remained stagnant. Positioning itself as a global leader in AI for medical imaging, Gleamer developed an innovative platform that assists radiologists by providing semi-automated pre-diagnoses of medical images.
By 2026, the platform was used by over 15,000 practitioners across 2,000 sites in 40 countries, processing more than 30 million medical exams annually. Gleamer raised a total of €36 million, including €27 million in 2023 from Supernova Invest and Heal Capital. In 2025, the company acquired Pixyl and Caerus Medical, becoming the sole AI provider covering all imaging modalities. Over 60% of its revenue is generated internationally, and it continues to expand its solutions for mammography, oncological scanning, and MRI.
Gleamer’s journey began in 2017 with a mission to reduce diagnostic errors amid a shortage of radiologists. Between 2022 and 2024, it entered a phase of massive international deployment, with over 650 institutions across 24 countries adopting its flagship solution, BoneView. In 2025, Gleamer transformed into a market consolidator by acquiring two medical imaging startups, Pixyl and Caerus Medical, expanding its expertise to brain and spinal MRIs. In March 2026, it was fully acquired by the American company RadNet (via its subsidiary DeepHealth) to integrate its global imaging network.
Gleamer’s value proposition centers on acting as a radiologist’s copilot, providing semi-automated diagnoses of lesions such as fractures and thoracic anomalies directly on X-rays. Its AI pre-writes medical reports in seconds, saving physicians valuable time. The platform is backed by nine major scientific publications and holds CE (Class IIa) and FDA certifications, ensuring clinical safety.

name: Ekimetric
description:
Fondée en 2006 par des diplômés de Polytechnique, Ekimetrics se spécialise dans l'IA décisionnelle appliquée au marketing et à la stratégie d'entreprise. Cette scale-up française aide les organisations à transformer leurs données en leviers stratégiques grâce à des algorithmes avancés et à la plateforme OneVision pour le Marketing Mix Modeling. Ekimetrics permet aux marques de mesurer, prévoir et optimiser leurs investissements marketing avec une approche holistique.

L'entreprise compte 400 experts en data science répartis dans quatre bureaux à Paris, Londres, New York et Hong Kong. Elle a réalisé plus de 1 000 projets de data science dans plus de 50 pays. Ekimetrics vise à tripler ses effectifs et son chiffre d'affaires d'ici 2028, avec l'objectif de générer près d'un tiers de ses revenus à l'international, principalement aux États-Unis. Reconnue comme leader dans le Magic Quadrant Gartner 2024 pour les solutions de Marketing Mix Modeling, la société génère annuellement plus d'un milliard de dollars de gains pour ses clients grâce à sa plateforme OneVision intégrant l'IA générative.

name: Zelros
description:
Créée en 2016, Zelros est une plateforme IA spécialisée dans le secteur de l'assurance, orientée sur les tactiques de vente. Véritable révolution de l'expérience client, elle offre une palette de services personnalisés et la souscription automatique. Les algorithmes de Zelros analysent le comportement des assurés pour recommander les produits les plus adaptés à leurs besoins.

Zelros emploie 60 salariés de plus de dix nationalités différentes et compte de nombreux clients comme le Crédit Agricole, Groupama, BPCE et la Matmut. L'entreprise poursuit son développement à l'international, notamment en Amérique du Nord, tout en consolidant son activité en Europe. En février 2021, elle a réalisé une levée de fonds de 11 millions de dollars. Au début de l'année 2025, Zelros a annoncé un partenariat stratégique avec IBM visant à réinventer les secteurs de la banque et de l'assurance avec la plateforme d'intelligence artificielle IBM watsonx.

name: Bodyguard.ai
description:
La startup Bodyguard.ai a été conçue pour lutter contre le cyberharcèlement, phénomène en croissance exponentielle lié à l'explosion du web. Pour protéger en temps réel les entreprises, les marques et les communautés de contenus malveillants et toxiques, l'entreprise met à leur disposition une solution de modération adaptable au format des réseaux sociaux et aux plateformes de toutes tailles. Bodyguard.ai s'engage également à préserver les supports web des spams, escroqueries et publicités indésirables.

Avec 80 salariés et plus de 600 millions d'utilisateurs dans le monde, Bodyguard.ai se développe dans de nombreux pays d'Europe tels que le Royaume-Uni, l'Italie et l'Espagne, mais aussi aux États-Unis. En 2022, la startup a effectué une levée de fonds de 9 millions d'euros pour sa solution de modération en ligne. En novembre 2024, elle a reçu le prix Action citoyenne & Civic Tech lors de la sixième édition des Tech For Good Awards.

name: Yseop
sector: AI model, Health & Social Care, ICT
description:
Spécialisée dans l'IA générative, Yseop fait partie des startups les plus reconnues du domaine de la recherche biomédicale, de la finance et des secteurs à risque. Depuis 2008, l'entreprise lyonnaise propose une solution de génération d'analyse et d'automatisation de rapports d'expertises, financiers et de gestion afin d'optimiser les tâches opérationnelles et le fonctionnement des activités de leurs clients.

En 2019, Yseop a réalisé une levée de fonds de plus de 8 millions d'euros pour accélérer son développement sur le marché américain. Récompensée à plusieurs reprises, la startup a été entre autres nominée aux World Technology Leader Awards en 2023 pour ses innovations dans le traitement du langage naturel appliqué aux données structurées.

name: Valeo.IA
description: Ses activités principales s’articulent autour de quatre grands axes : 1. La perception 3D et la conduite autonomeL’équipe conçoit des algorithmes de vision par ordinateur pour analyser l’environnement de la voiture à 360° en temps réel :Interprétation de scènes complexes : L'IA identifie les piétons, cyclistes, véhicules et obstacles.Modélisation prédictive : Elle anticipe les comportements (par exemple, déterminer si un piéton va traverser le trottoir) pour valider des trajectoires sûres.Fusion de capteurs : Les modèles croisent les flux de données issus des caméras, des radars et des LiDARs de Valeo. 2. L’apprentissage efficace (Data-Efficient Learning)Pour entraîner les intelligences artificielles sans dépendre de volumes massifs de données humaines déjà triées (parfois impossibles ou trop longues à obtenir), Valeo.ai mène des recherches sur :L’apprentissage auto-supervisé (Self-supervised learning) : Permettre à l'IA d'apprendre par elle-même directement à partir de données brutes non labellisées.La génération de scénarios via l'IA Générative : Créer artificiellement des milliers de variantes de routes à partir d'une seule scène réelle en modifiant la météo ou en ajoutant des obstacles rares pour tester virtuellement la sécurité de la voiture. 3. Des modèles d'IA de confiance et explicablesLes systèmes embarqués dans l'automobile doivent être irréprochables et sécurisés. Les chercheurs conçoivent des modèles dits "dépendables" :Explicabilité : Fournir une traçabilité claire sur les raisons pour lesquelles l'IA a pris une décision complexe à un moment T.Élimination des biais : Anticiper et éliminer les erreurs algorithmiques ou les comportements imprévisibles liés aux biais des données d'entraînement. 4. L’Open Innovation et les publications scientifiquesValeo.ai ne garde pas ses recherches secrètes, mais fonctionne comme un laboratoire académique :Publications de classe mondiale : Le centre publie régulièrement ses travaux dans les plus grands congrès internationaux de vision par ordinateur et d'IA (CVPR, ICCV, etc.).Partages open-source : Les équipes publient du code en accès libre pour faire progresser la communauté scientifique mondiale.Partenariats académiques : Ils collaborent étroitement avec de prestigieux laboratoires d'universités françaises et internationales, et encadrent de nombreux doctorants (PhD)

name: Volta medical
sector: AI model, Health & Social Care, Cardio
description: Volta Medical est une MedTech française pionnière, spécialisée dans le développement de logiciels d'intelligence artificielle (IA) appliqués à l'électrophysiologie cardiaque. Fondée en 2016 à Marseille par Théophile Mohr Durdez (data scientist) et trois cardiologues rythmologues (les Dr Julien Seitz, Jérôme Kalifa et Clément Bars), l'entreprise aide les chirurgiens à traiter les troubles complexes du rythme cardiaque, en ciblant prioritairement la fibrillation auriculaire (FA).

name: Prophesee
description:
Prophesee: Pioneering Neuromorphic Event-Based Vision for Ultra-Fast Sensing
Founded in 2016 and originally known as Chronocam, Prophesee is a pioneer in neuromorphic event-based vision. The startup has developed bio-inspired sensors that mimic the human eye, detecting only pixel-level changes in brightness rather than capturing full images. This revolutionary approach drastically reduces the amount of data processed while achieving microsecond-level temporal resolution, making it ideal for observing fast-moving phenomena.
Since 2018, Prophesee has partnered with Sony to co-develop fourth-generation event-based sensors, the IMX636 and IMX637, which are now mass-produced by the Japanese giant. The company employs over 130 engineers across Paris, Grenoble, Shanghai, Tokyo, and Silicon Valley. In 2023, Prophesee raised €50 million, with participation from Xiaomi, and in 2024, it announced a €15 million investment to develop the next generation of neuromorphic AI for smartphones.
Prophesee’s Metavision technology is already powering applications in industrial robotics, automotive systems, IoT, and augmented reality, supported by a network of over 15,000 partners and developers.
main_investors: Bpifrance (fonds Large Venture), Sony Innovation Fund, Xiaomi, Intel Capital, Bosch Venture Capital, iBionext.

name: Mindee
description: Fondée en 2018, Mindee se spécialise dans l'automatisation du traitement de documents grâce à l'intelligence artificielle. La startup permet aux développeurs de construire et d'intégrer en quelques clics des solutions d'extraction de données textuelles sur n'importe quel type de document ou photo, même de mauvaise qualité. Mindee répond à deux enjeux majeurs : l'optimisation des processus métiers de traitement documentaire et l'amélioration de l'expérience utilisateur via le remplissage automatique de formulaires.L'entreprise a levé 2 millions d'euros en 2019 auprès de Serena et Bpifrance pour développer sa plateforme d'API d'extraction de données. Mindee propose des modèles pré-entraînés pour différents types de documents (factures, reçus, passeports, fiches de paie) et permet également de créer des modèles personnalisés via son outil DocTI. En 2024, la startup a développé des LLM propriétaires et un algorithme de graphe intelligent permettant d'atteindre une précision de niveau humain sur l'extraction de documents financiers.

name: Indium
description: L'objectif central de teX.ai est d'automatiser entièrement la transformation de données textuelles brutes et non structurées en informations claires, structurées et exploitables par les entreprises. Sa technologie s'articule autour de trois modules principaux :Extraction de texte (Text Extraction) : Il repère et extrait de manière autonome les données clés (comme des numéros de lots, des dates, des tableaux complexes) au sein de documents volumineux, de PDF ou d'images de factures, indépendamment de leur disposition visuelle.Classification de texte (Text Classification) : L'algorithme trie et catégorise automatiquement de grands volumes de données (tels que des tickets de support client, des plaintes, des descriptions de produits ou des flux de commentaires).Résumé de texte (Text Summarization) : Il utilise des modèles de Deep Learning pour condenser de longs rapports d'investisseurs, des revues scientifiques, des documents financiers ou juridiques en synthèses courtes et faciles à lire. Indium software, Indium après rachat.

name: Nabla
description:
Founded by experts from Facebook AI Research (FAIR), Nabla has established itself as the leader in generative AI assistants for medical practitioners. The startup automates clinical documentation to give doctors more time for patient care.
Nabla was founded in 2018 by Alex LeBrun (former AI leader at Facebook), Delphine Groll, and Martin Raison. Between 2021 and 2023, the company successfully pivoted toward ambient clinical reporting, where AI listens to and synthesizes patient consultations. In 2024-2025, Nabla experienced hypergrowth in the United States, which now accounts for 95% of its market. In July 2026, the company structured its American governance by appointing Brian Manning as its new global CEO to orchestrate its scaling phase.
Nabla’s value proposition revolves around its ambient AI for consultations, which captures doctor-patient conversations and generates structured medical reports in seconds. Through an exclusive partnership with Advanced Machine Intelligence (Yann LeCun’s research lab), Nabla integrates cutting-edge technologies, such as "world models," to automate complex hospital workflows. This innovation drastically reduces administrative time, cutting secretarial tasks in half and saving healthcare professionals 1 to 2 hours per day.

name: Microchip Technology Inc
description: La Scission (1987-1989) : L'histoire commence en 1987 lorsque le géant industriel General Instrument décide de filialiser sa division microélectronique en difficulté. En 1989, la structure devient totalement indépendante sous le nom de Microchip Technology après son rachat par un groupe de capital-risqueurs.Le virage des 8-bits et l'ère Sanghi (1990-1993) : Au début des années 1990, l'entreprise frôle la faillite. Steve Sanghi prend la direction et prend un pari à contre-courant : délaisser la course aux processeurs 32-bits coûteux pour lancer des microcontrôleurs 8-bits (les célèbres séries PIC) très bon marché (vendus à l'époque 2,40 $ l'unité). L'entreprise entre en bourse (NASDAQ) en 1993.L'expansion par acquisitions (2010-Aujourd'hui) : Devenue une véritable machine à profits, Microchip enchaîne les rachats stratégiques pour enrichir son catalogue de technologies : Silicon Storage Technology (SST) en 2010, Micrel en 2015, et surtout le rachat massif d'Atmel en 2016 (mettant la main sur l'architecture concurrente AVR, cerveau des cartes Arduino).Aujourd'hui : Microchip est passée du statut de start-up moribonde à celui de titan des puces électroniques, fournissant plus de 100 000 produits différents à environ 125 000 clients industriels, automobiles et aéronautiques à travers le monde
